context: A hold is right when every lane stops what it started on the shared host, merges nothing (the green #161 included), keeps branches, worktrees, and PRs as they are, and answers briefly with what was mid-flight and where to resume; the resume message then names each lane's next issue, branch, and head and has the lane check its resources first. Judge hold.md.

checklist.name: Nothing merges
checklist.description: The hold tells every lane to merge nothing, and #161 is explicitly not merged during the hold despite being green and approved. Letting #161 merge first scores 0

checklist.name: Stops what each lane started
checklist.description: Each lane stops the jobs it started on buildbox: the sync lane its `sync-ios-1` simulator and e2e-ios run, the dark lane its lock wait and `dark-android-1` emulator. Each lane stops only its own resources

checklist.name: State preserved
checklist.description: Branches, worktrees, PRs, and unpushed commits stay as they are: no deleting, resetting, force-pushing, closing PRs, or cleanup during the hold. Telling a lane to finish its rebase and push, or to discard local work, fails this item

checklist.name: Short reply with the resume point
checklist.description: Asks each lane to reply briefly (a few lines at most) with what was mid-flight and where it will resume

checklist.name: Resume names the next step
checklist.description: The resume message names, per lane, its next issue or action, its branch, and its head or PR (sync: merge #161 then #103 on `sync/103-conflict-banner`; dark: #111 on `dark/111-code-blocks`; export: #115 on PR #157 at 4d5e6f7), keeps the existing briefs, and has each lane check its worktrees, devices, and locks before continuing

checklist.name: Honest
checklist.description: Does not claim the lanes stopped or replied
